stories.headline: Open-Source Diabetes Management Tool Built with AI Gains Traction
stories.summary: GlycemicGPT, an open-source AI-powered diabetes management application, has garnered attention on Hacker News with 64 points and active community discussion [1]. The project represents another example of healthcare applications being built using AI capabilities.
stories.impact: This showcases how developers are leveraging AI tools to address specific healthcare needs, potentially inspiring similar community-driven health applications.

sources.title: Show HN: GlycemicGPT – Open-source AI-powered diabetes management

stories.headline: Community Discusses Anthropic Platform Issues
stories.summary: A Twitter thread about Anthropic-related concerns has sparked significant discussion on Hacker News, drawing 82 comments and 63 upvotes [1]. The nature of the 'kerfuffle' suggests ongoing community dialogue about the platform.
stories.impact: Platform discussions like these often reflect broader user sentiment and can influence how the community approaches Claude-based development.

stories.headline: Use `claude plugin prune` to clean up orphaned plugin dependencies
stories.summary: Auto-installed plugin dependencies can accumulate over time, taking up disk space. The prune command removes dependencies that are no longer needed by any installed plugins.
actionable_steps: Run `claude plugin prune` in your terminal
Alternatively, use `claude plugin uninstall --prune [plugin-name]` to uninstall a plugin and clean up its dependencies in one step

stories.headline: Write a CLAUDE.md file to set project conventions once
stories.summary: Adding a CLAUDE.md to your project root lets you define coding standards, test commands, and architectural decisions that persist across every Claude Code session. Think of it as onboarding documentation that Claude reads automatically — you teach it once instead of repeating yourself.
actionable_steps: Create a CLAUDE.md in your project root with build/test/lint commands
Add coding conventions like naming patterns, preferred libraries, and file structure
Include architectural decisions and constraints Claude should respect
Use /init in Claude Code to auto-generate a starter CLAUDE.md

stories.headline: Use `/team-onboarding` command to generate teammate ramp-up guides
stories.summary: Claude Code can automatically create onboarding documentation for new team members based on your local usage patterns. This saves time creating training materials and ensures consistency in how team members learn your workflows.
actionable_steps: Update to Claude Code v2.1.101 or later
Run the `/team-onboarding` command in your Claude Code interface
Review the generated ramp-up guide and customize as needed
Share the guide with new team members

stories.headline: Use visual mode in Claude Code for text selection and editing
stories.summary: Claude Code now supports vim-style visual mode (v) and visual-line mode (V) for selecting and manipulating text. This enables more efficient text editing workflows similar to vim editors.
actionable_steps: Press 'v' to enter visual mode for character-by-character selection
Press 'V' to enter visual-line mode for line-by-line selection
Use standard vim operators on your selected text

stories.headline: Use ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H to extend prompt cache duration
stories.summary: Setting this environment variable enables 1-hour prompt cache TTL instead of the default, which can reduce API costs and improve response times for longer coding sessions. This works across API key, Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry deployments.
actionable_steps: Set the environment variable ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=true in your system or deployment configuration
Restart Claude Code to apply the new caching setting
Monitor your usage to verify extended caching is working
